clue.text: Put in order for tape

indicators.note: one thing being put in another means its letters go inside that other word

blocks.note: a caste is a social order or class
to set something down is to put it there

explanation.surface: An instruction to file away a tape in proper sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in order' reads as one phrase meaning arrange, but 'in' is the insertion signal splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a plastic case holding magnetic recording tape, so the word can stand for the tape itself.

clue.text: Talk about capacity

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
wearing a given hat means acting in a given capacity or role

explanation.surface: A talk on the subject of volume or capacity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capacity' suggests volume; it means a role, as in 'wearing my other hat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally, a straightforward synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Tool, last of screwdrivers I removed from bag

indicators.note: the last of a word is just its final letter
something removed from a word is taken out of it

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
a pannier is a bag slung on a bicycle or a pack animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A toolbag with the screwdrivers taken out, leaving a different tool.
explanation.walkthrough: A pannier is a bag hung either side of a bicycle wheel or a donkey's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanner is a hand implement for turning nuts and bolts, the British word for a wrench.

clue.text: Taste mine poured out in café

indicators.note: liquid poured out spills every which way, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A customer offering a sip of their drink in a café.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or bistro, a kind of café selling drinks.

clue.text: Methane plant he destroyed in film

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A movie in which a man blows up a gas plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elephant Man is David Lynch's 1980 movie about Joseph Merrick, so it is one example of a film.

clue.text: Computer circuit (main)

blocks.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
the main or chief thing is the top one

explanation.surface: A computer described as a circuit board, with 'main' in brackets as if a technical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer, an example of the wider class.

clue.text: Some latticework in cockloft

indicators.note: some of a word is only a part of it, so the letters sit inside it

blocks.note: letters two to six of this word

explanation.surface: Wooden lattice panels up in the roof space.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockloft is an old word for a small loft just under the roof ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockloft is a small upper loft, the room directly under the roof, which is what an attic is.

clue.text: Violent wind encountered on the way over - destructive thing

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means heading upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to have encountered someone is to have met them
a pest is a creature that does damage

explanation.surface: A storm met on a journey, described as a destroyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm with strong winds, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Insecticide used in capital, eco-friendly

blocks.note: Paris is the capital of France
green means environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: A pesticide sprayed in a city, billed as environmentally safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that Paris green is a highly toxic copper and arsenic compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris green is a poisonous emerald pigment once widely used as an insecticide and rat poison.

clue.text: Sharp, involved with a soldier, gets round husband in novel

definitions.note: A Shropshire Lad is actually a cycle of poems, not a novel

indicators.note: things involved are tangled up, so these letters are mixed together
letters that get round something surround it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A sharp soldier circles round a husband in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: Housman's A Shropshire Lad is a poetry collection, so 'novel' is loose; Shropshire is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shropshire Lad is A. E. Housman's 1896 book of verse, a literary work named after the English county.

clue.text: A fraction to one side

blocks.note: taken as written
a fraction of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: A mathematical fraction pushed off to the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set apart is placed aside, separated from the rest, as an adverb.

clue.text: Stem a riot developing in Asian country

indicators.note: a situation developing is changing shape, so these letters take a new form

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Riot police told to contain trouble breaking out somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: East Timor (Timor-Leste) is a south-east Asian nation occupying half of the island of Timor.

clue.text: Creature with nuts in film

indicators.note: one thing coming with another means the two sit side by side

blocks.note: an animal is a living creature
both words are informal for mad

explanation.surface: A film scene featuring a creature eating nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' tempts you towards food; it means crazy. Animal Crackers is a 1930 Marx Brothers comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal Crackers is the title of a Marx Brothers movie, so the answer is one example of a film.

clue.text: Struggle at university? Tall Sikh's struggling

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing around, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a British student in residence at university is said to be up
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tall Sikh student finding university life hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Sikh's' stands for 'is', joining wordplay to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An uphill task is an idiom for a hard job requiring sustained effort, a struggle.

clue.text: Cut cut and cut a root vegetable

indicators.note: a word that is cut short loses its last letter

blocks.note: to pare is to cut or trim
a snip is a small cut

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction stuttering over chopping a root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition looks like nonsense: the first word gives PARE, the second trims it to PAR, the third gives SNIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The parsnip is a pale tapering taproot eaten as a vegetable, an example of the class.

clue.text: Dog tip

blocks.note: first meaning: a gun dog breed that stands still facing the game
second meaning: a hint or piece of advice

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a dog being tipped over, but the two words are separate meanings of one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a breed of hunting dog, and also a helpful suggestion or hint given to someone.

clue.text: While being conveyed in it, rants disconcertingly

indicators.note: something done disconcertingly throws things into disarray, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A passenger ranting alarmingly while being driven along.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged word does not stay where the clue puts it: it slots between the two short words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods in transit are on the way, travelling from one place to another, i.e. being carried.

clue.text: At home, unusually irate, showing a disinclination to move

indicators.note: something done unusually is done in an odd way, so these letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: someone at home is in
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at home, oddly angry and refusing to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency to stay put, a reluctance to act or change, matching the noun phrase.

clue.text: The most distinctive element of a German city church

blocks.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The chief feature of a church in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its core nature, the quality most characteristic of it.

clue.text: Direct phone link arranged in hotel

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A direct telephone line set up in a hotel room.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a dedicated telephone line giving immediate contact, for instance between heads of state.

clue.text: Pick out one terribly behindhand

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
terribly late is so late

explanation.surface: Singling out the one person who is always running late.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to separate and identify it from the rest, much as picking out does.

clue.text: Hear serious crime involves ring - be persuaded to act sensibly

indicators.note: a thing that involves another takes it in, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: to hear is to listen
treason is a grave crime against the state
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A court hearing on a grave crime involving a crime ring, with a plea for sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring goes in after the first letter of the crime, not in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen to reason is an idiom for accepting sensible advice and acting accordingly.

clue.text: A happening, constant over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, being over something means sitting above it, so this part comes first

blocks.note: even means steady or constant
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something that keeps happening steadily over a period.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that takes place, which is what a happening is.

clue.text: Work produced by Poe, unfinished, upset America

indicators.note: a thing left unfinished is missing its ending
in a down clue, set upward means turned upside down, so the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A work by Edgar Allan Poe, left incomplete, that offended Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's name is cut first and only then turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition, Latin for a piece of work.

clue.text: Picture girl by lobby

indicators.note: one thing by another sits next to it, so these parts are placed side by side

blocks.note: a girl's name
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: A photograph of a girl standing in a lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' suggests a photo; here it means a motion picture, the 1977 Woody Allen film.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Hall is a Woody Allen movie, and picture is a common word for a film.

clue.text: Scallywag has most of seafood

indicators.note: most of something is all but its final part

blocks.note: scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a seafood dish

explanation.surface: A rascal grabbing most of the seafood platter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rogue, a near synonym of scallywag.

clue.text: Stand by tower, closed

blocks.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: A guard standing beside a tower that has been shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand by' looks like being next to the tower, but it is the definition: to stick to a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep to an agreement is to honour it, the same idiom as standing by it.

clue.text: Newspaper boss, first from Eton, strides out

indicators.note: the first from a word is only its opening letter
letters set out are spread around and reordered

blocks.note: Eton is a famous English boarding school
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief, Eton-educated, marching out of the office.
explanation.definitionFit: An editress is a dated term for a woman editor, who runs a newspaper.
